newsitem.title: USA: Sears ups bid, to merge with MaxServ.
newsitem.headline: Sears ups bid, to merge with MaxServ.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co and MaxServ Inc said Monday they reached a definitive merger agreement in which Sears agreed to raise the price of its offer for MaxServ shares to $7.75 each from $7.00.

MaxServ provides information services for Sears customers and for the reapir and servicing of appliances and electronics by Sears Home Services technicians. Sears accounts for more than 90 percent of MaxServ's revenues.

The expiration date of the increased offer will be extended until March 14, 1997. Sears said it intends to distribute today to MaxServ shareholders a supplement to its prior offer to purchase, dated February 4, 1997.

At a meeting held yesterday, the Special Committee of the Board of Directors of MaxServ unanimously recommended approval of the merger agreement and determined that the $7.75 per share offer is fair to and in the best interests of the stockholders of MaxServ.
The Special Committee has recommended that MaxServ shareholders tender their shares in the offer.
The members of the Special Committee have agreed to tender all of the shares over which they have dispositive power, including 1,014,800 shares owned by two investment funds.

Jane Thompson, president of Sears Home Services, said "Sears is pleased to have reached an agreement with MaxServ. It has been Sears' desire from the outset to negotiate a friendly transaction with the Special Committee."
Sears, the second largest retailer in the U.S., has annual revenues of more than $38 billion.
Sears had launched on February 4 its first ever hostile takeover, of MaxServ, after MaxServ rejected its $7 a share offer.
